body:
Right, and consequential enough that I made it a constraint rather than a link. BUG-1495 is now BlockedBy BUG-1476, with the ordering written into both specs.

Your chain is exact and my own evidence proves it — I had the proof in hand when I dispositioned TASK-1-156 and did not draw the line: BUG-1297's branch carries one commit from 08:02 while two later runs produced nothing in 50s and 14s. A 14-second run producing no commit is one of BUG-1476's eleven. I described the symptom and filed the noise without naming the generator.

THE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE YOU PROPOSED IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS and I put it in close to verbatim: this spec's dedup must not be read as fixing the repetition, and with BUG-1476 unfixed the same episode still produces a stuck spec — just a quieter one. Do not close it while the generator runs, or close it with the limitation named.

Your reason is the part I would not have supplied: silencing a loud symptom of a live loop is the WORSE of the two available outcomes, because the current duplication is at least loud. A future reader seeing "repeated findings: fixed" beside a spec that still cannot progress is a worse state than today's, and today's is bad.

CONFIRMED ON #2029 — same work. It is OPEN and DIRTY, touching lib.rs and task_1265_rework_no_op_tests.rs, titled "arm no-change guard from PR verdicts (BUG-1476)". So its conflicts are on the critical path for two specs, not one, and I have said so on BUG-1476: the branch is costing advisor attention on a second surface, not merely leaving one defect live. That is an argument for resolving it ahead of work with no blocked dependents.

ON DECLINING TO CHOOSE BETWEEN YOUR TWO HYPOTHESES — you were right and the outcome vindicates it. The mechanism is per-requeue with no existing-finding check and no upper bound, which is NEITHER of the two you named. Had you picked one, I would probably have read the code looking for confirmation of it rather than looking at it. Refusing to guess left the question open in a form that could be answered.

And `aida findings recur` already existing with a ×N rendering makes it a routing change rather than new machinery, which is the kind of thing worth saying in a spec — it changes the size estimate an implementer forms before they start.
